TargetRLF1: Fertilization: Fertilization occurs when a sperm cell meets an egg cell in one of the fallopian tubes. This usually happens during sexual intercourse. When a sperm penetrates the egg, their genetic material combines to form a zygote, which is the first cell of a new individual. Pregnancy: After fertilization, the zygote begins to divide rapidly as it travels down the fallopian tube toward the uterus. It becomes a blastocyst and implants itself into the lining of the uterus. The blastocyst then develops into an embryo and later into a fetus. The pregnancy continues until the fetus is ready for birth, which typically occurs around 40 weeks from the last menstrual period. During pregnancy, the female body undergoes numerous changes to support the developing fetus, including hormonal changes, increased blood volume, and changes in the uterus to accommodate the growing baby. These processes are essential for human reproduction and the continuation of life.

TargetRLF1: A chlamydia also known as Chlamydial Genitourinary infection test detects the bacteria that cause chlamydia, a sexually transmitted infection (STI). Or they may use a cell culture to see how chlamydia treatments are working. Because of the possibility of multiple sexually transmitted infections, all patients with any sexually transmitted disease (STD) should be evaluated for chlamydial infection. There are no risks involved with these tests. Rarely the results of the tests may be inconclusive or unclear and you may need to give another sample.

Common oral herpes symptoms include blisters (cold sores) or open sores (ulcers) in or around the mouth or lips. Most people notice a group or cluster of blisters or ulcers (lesions). Herpes is a lifelong sexually transmitted infection, that cannot be cured. However, the number of outbreaks/recurrences may reduce over time.

TargetRLF1: Human immunodeficiency virus is a zoonosis – an infection that originated in animals and passed into human hosts. It is closely related to the simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) found in chimpanzees in central Africa. Over the decades, the disease has spread all over the world.

TargetRLF1: Human immunodeficiency virus is a zoonosis – an infection that originated in animals and passed into human hosts. It is closely related to the simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) found in chimpanzees in central Africa. To date, the earliest known case of HIV-1 infection in human blood is from a sample taken in 1959 from a man who'd died in Kinshasa in what was then the Belgian Congo. SIV probably entered the human population as a result of hunting chimpanzees. It is plausible that transmission could have occurred through a hunter being wounded and blood from a chimpanzee entering his bloodstream. Chimpanzees avoid humans wherever possible, so it is likely that SIVcpz crossed into humans as a result of human encroachment into forest areas. The origin of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) has been a subject of scientific research and debate since the virus was identified in the 1980s. It came to global attention after doctors started receiving reports of rare cases of pneumonia, cancer and other illnesses in young gay homosexual men and injection drug users. Over the decades, the disease has spread all over the world.

HIV primarily infects specific immune cells in the body called CD4+ T cells, and it does not have a preference for a particular blood group. HIV is primarily transmitted through contact with certain body fluids, including blood, semen, vaginal fluids, rectal fluids, and breast milk, that contain a high concentration of the virus. The risk of HIV infection is related to behaviors and practices that expose individuals to the virus, rather than their blood type.

If you are sexually active, you can do the following things to lower your chances of getting Genital Herpes or Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), also known as herpes:•        Being in a long-term mutually monogamous relationship with a partner who does not have herpes.•        Using condoms the right way every time you have sex.Be aware that not all herpes sores occur in areas that a condom can cover. It is important that you avoid getting genital herpes during pregnancy. Tell your healthcare provider if you have ever had a genital herpes diagnosis or symptoms. Also tell them about any possible exposure to genital herpes. If you have genital herpes, you may need to take anti-herpes medicine towards the end of your pregnancy. This medicine may reduce your risk of having signs or symptoms of genital herpes when you deliver. At the time of delivery, your healthcare provider should carefully examine you for herpes sores. If you have signs or symptoms of genital herpes at delivery, a 'C-section' is likely to occur.

TargetRLF1: Human immunodeficiency virus is a zoonosis – an infection that originated in animals and passed into human hosts. It is closely related to the simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV) found in chimpanzees in central Africa. SIV probably entered the human population as a result of hunting chimpanzees. It is plausible that transmission could have occurred through a hunter being wounded and blood from a chimpanzee entering his bloodstream. Chimpanzees avoid humans wherever possible, so it is likely that SIVcpz crossed into humans as a result of human encroachment into forest areas. The origin of the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) has been a subject of scientific research and debate since the virus was identified in the 1980s. It came to global attention after doctors started receiving reports of rare cases of pneumonia, cancer and other illnesses in young gay homosexual men and injection drug users. Over the decades, the disease has spread all over the world.

Over the decades, the disease has spread all over the world.

The organism that causes the disease was first discovered in 1879 in Albert Neisser, hence the organisma being called Neisseria Gonorrhoea. The word Gonorrhea itself derives from the Greek, meaning "the flow of seed" (gono: seed, rhea: flow).

TargetRLF1: While some people with Genital Herpes or Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV), also known as herpes will never have any symptoms, other people can develop symptoms within a few weeks of being infected. Common oral herpes symptoms include blisters (cold sores) or open sores (ulcers) in or around the mouth or lips. Most people notice a group or cluster of blisters or ulcers (lesions). These lesions burn and can be painful. They can appear on the buttocks, anus or thighs, on the vulva or vagina in women, and on the penis or scrotum in men. Often, before the lesions appear, patients describe a prodrome, characterized by a tingling or burning sensation in the area where the lesions will develop that can be noticed during urination, along with itching or discomfort in the genital area. You can also have the following symptoms, Blisters on the mouth or lips, Fever, headache or pain in the joints, Trouble urinating. In case of Neonatal Herpes, signs that your baby may have herpes are:irritability, blisters anywhere on her body, trouble breathing, grunting, blue appearance (cyanosis), rapid breathing, short periods of no breathing, jaundice, bleeding easily. People can have repeated outbreaks over time (‘recurrences’). These are usually shorter and less severe than the first outbreak. Herpes is a lifelong sexually transmitted infection, that cannot be cured. However, the number of outbreaks/recurrences may reduce over time.

This test tells you if you have the chlamydia infection so that you can get treat treatment and avoid complications.. You should get tested regularly if you have unprotected sex with a new partner, multiple partners or a partner who has an STI. You should also get tested if you have symptoms or you are pregnant. Many people with Chlamydia don't have symptoms. Because of the possibility of multiple sexually transmitted infections, all patients with any sexually transmitted disease (STD) should be evaluated for chlamydial infection.

TargetRLF1: Gonorrhea can be traced back to the earliest records of the human race. The Romans, Jews and Arabs all have documents referring to gonorrhea and each society had their own description of symptoms and treatment. The origins of Gonorrhea can be traced back to the Old Testament in the books of Leviticus and Genesis where it is described as a contagious, continuous emission of semen and painful erection. The disease has been referred to by various names in different societies. The Roman physician Galen in 130 AD described the disease as an "involuntary escape of semen".   Hippocrates (460–375 BC) called in "Strangury." The disease was also referred to as “The Clap,” referring either to the “clapping” sensation experienced by the infected person during urination or, as others believe, as a derivative of the French brothels, known as “Les Clapiers,” where the disease was quite rampant. In those days, men were considered victims and women as the source of the disease. The organism that causes the disease was first discovered in 1879 in Albert Neisser, hence the organisma being called Neisseria Gonorrhoea. The word Gonorrhea itself derives from the Greek, meaning "the flow of seed" (gono: seed, rhea: flow).

TargetRLF1: Herpes can only be diagnosed at a health centre. You cannot test for it at home or using radiological methods. Blood tests do not actually detect the virus but look for antibodies.

TargetRLF1: A chlamydia also known as Chlamydial Genitourinary infection test detects the bacteria that cause chlamydia, a sexually transmitted infection (STI). This test tells you if you have the chlamydia infection so that you can get treat treatment and avoid complications. Your provider takes a sample of urine or secretions from your vagina, penis or rectum and sends it to a lab for testing using a test called NAATs (short for nucleic acid amplification tests), which is very accurate and easy to take. Results are usually ready in a day. Less often, providers use a cell culture to test for chlamydia. In this case, your provider swabs your vagina, urethra or anus to collect a sample of fluid and cells. They send the cells to a lab to test. If bacteria are present, they will grow, which indicates an infection. Providers may choose this type of chlamydia test to detect infections in the anus. Or they may use a cell culture to see how chlamydia treatments are working. Because of the possibility of multiple sexually transmitted infections, all patients with any sexually transmitted disease (STD) should be evaluated for chlamydial infection. There are no risks involved with these tests. Rarely the results of the tests may be inconclusive or unclear and you may need to give another sample.

Ni muhimu kutambua kwamba wakati wa kutumia PrEP kwa kuzuia virusi vya ukimwi, bado kuna hatari ya kuambukizwa magonjwa ya zinaa kama vile klamidia, kisonono, kaswende, au herpes. Ili kujikinga na magonjwa ya zinaa, ni muhimu kuchukua hatua zinazofaa za kuzuia, zikiwemo: Matumizi ya kondomu, Kupata vipimo vya magonjwa ya zinaa, Mawasiliano na wenzi wa ngono, Kujifunza kuhusu magonjwa ya zinaa, na Kutumia dawa za kuzuia magonjwa ya zinaa. Kwa muhtasari, PrEP ni nzuri katika kuzuia maambukizi ya virusi vya ukimwi lakini haitoi kinga dhidi ya magonjwa ya zinaa. Kwa hivyo, ni muhimu kuchukua hatua za ziada za kuzuia ili kujikinga na magonjwa ya zinaa wakati wa shughuli za ngono.
